issues.body:
`_resolve_targets` used to execute the shipped resolver as `__main__`, so the resolver's OWN environment read and OWN emitter were the code under test. The new harness bypasses both:

    namespace = {"__name__": "backfill_targets"}
    exec(_resolver_src, namespace)
    result = namespace["resolve_file"]("policy/repos.toml", os.environ.get("REQUESTED", ""))
    with contextlib.redirect_stdout(buffer):
        print("repos=" + json.dumps(result))

The harness now reads REQUESTED and formats `repos=` itself, so neither is asserted about the shipped code.

`REQUESTED` is consumed in exactly ONE place in the whole tree — scripts/backfill-targets.py:114:

    requested = os.environ.get("REQUESTED", "") if args.requested is None else args.requested

and nothing tests it:
- backfill-targets.py `_self_test` calls `main(["--policy", ..., "--requested", ...])`, so `args.requested is not None` and the env branch is never taken.
- `_resolve_step_result` pins `env = {..., "REQUESTED": ""}` and only exercises the full-sweep and none-enabled fixtures, never a requested target.
- The `resolver_requested_binding` seam row only proves the YAML binds `REQUESTED: ${{ inputs.target_repo }}`; it cannot prove anything READS it.

LIVE MUTANT: rewrite line 114 as `requested = args.requested or ""` (or bind `TARGET_REPO` instead of `REQUESTED`). Both `--self-test` suites stay 100% green, and a human dispatching `target_repo: owner/x` with `apply=true` gets an apply-run against EVERY enabled policy repo instead of the one they named — the widening direction, and the failure class #1544/sol-r1 exist to kill. This is a relaxation of an existing trust check: the mutant was killed before this diff and is alive after it, and the rows "a requested ENABLED target narrows the matrix to exactly that one repo" / "a requested DISABLED target is REFUSED" now read as end-to-end coverage they no longer provide.
issues.fix_hint:
Route `_resolve_targets` back through the shipped entry point so the env read and the emitter are the code under test. Inside the temp cwd, with REQUESTED set/unset exactly as now, do something like:

    namespace = {"__name__": "backfill_targets"}
    exec(_resolver_src, namespace)
    with contextlib.redirect_stdout(buffer), contextlib.redirect_stderr(io.StringIO()):
        status = namespace["main"]([])          # NO --policy, NO --requested: both defaults
    if status != 0:
        return "REFUSED"

with `main([])` relying on the default `--policy policy/repos.toml` and on `REQUESTED` from the environment. That restores the kill on line 114, on the `repos=` output NAME, on the JSON encoding, and on the refusal->nonzero conversion for the requested-target fixtures (today only the sweep and none-enabled fixtures reach `main`, via the shell seam). Equivalently, run it as a subprocess: `subprocess.run([sys.executable, "scripts/backfill-targets.py"], cwd=workdir, env={**os.environ, "REQUESTED": requested or ""}, ...)`. Either way the existing `except BaseException` / TargetResolutionError special-case becomes unnecessary, since `main` already converts the refusal into a nonzero status.
issues.title: Refactor drops the only coverage of the REQUESTED env read — a manual single-target dispatch can silently widen to a full sweep with every self-test green

issues.fix_hint: Prefer `namespace.get("TargetResolutionError")` and an `isinstance` check, e.g. `_err = namespace.get("TargetResolutionError"); if isinstance(_err, type) and isinstance(exc, _err): return "REFUSED"`. Better still, this branch disappears entirely once `_resolve_targets` goes through `main()` per the blocker above, because a refusal is then just a nonzero return status.
issues.title: Refusal detection matches an exception by string name, weakening the REFUSED/ABORTED distinction

issues.fix_hint: Update the three comments/strings to describe the script-invocation seam ("the resolve step runs a checked-in helper; every non-blank line here IS a command the runner's shell executes"), and reword the compile-failure reason to name backfill-targets.py.
issues.title: Comments and a refusal reason still describe a heredoc that no longer exists

verdict.summary:
Extracting the targets resolver from the heredoc into scripts/backfill-targets.py is a good move: the helper is stdlib-only, fail-closed (`enabled is True`, refuses unknown/disabled/empty selections), listed in scripts/selftest-suite.txt, carries a non-vacuous --self-test, is added to the thin sparse-checkout, and the new `resolver_checkout_paths` + updated `resolver_shell_commands`/`resolver_emits_to_step_output` seam rows exact-match the new command sequence. The shell-seam rows (`_resolve_step_result`) still run the shipped `run:` block end-to-end and pin both directions of the exit status, so pipefail coverage survives.

But the refactor RELAXES the executed-resolver self-test in a way that leaves a fail-open mutant alive. Previously `_resolve_targets` did `exec(_resolver_src, {"__name__": "__main__"})`, so the shipped code's own `os.environ.get("REQUESTED")` read and its own `print("repos="+json.dumps(...))` emitter were under test. Now the harness calls `namespace["resolve_file"](...)` directly, reads REQUESTED itself, and prints the `repos=` line itself. `REQUESTED` is consumed in exactly one place in the tree (scripts/backfill-targets.py:114) and no test in either file exercises that line: backfill-targets.py's own self-test always passes `--requested` explicitly, and `_resolve_step_result` pins `REQUESTED: ""`. So changing line 114 to ignore the environment leaves BOTH suites fully green while a manual `workflow_dispatch` with `target_repo: owner/x` silently widens to an apply-sweep of every enabled repo — the widening direction the rows named "narrows the matrix to exactly that one repo" and "a requested DISABLED target is REFUSED" claim to guard. Those two rows now test the library function, not the shipped dispatch path.

No security regressions otherwise: no token-shaped material, permissions still `{}` on `targets`, checkout still SHA-pinned with `persist-credentials: false`, and no untrusted text is expanded into the shell.
